notes: Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: match.variant (catalogue variant; null matches any) and preferred (true = recommended recipe when several share a match). No Windows/macOS recipe was run; only Linux.
user_site_leak: Every recipe except the embeddable zip (whose ._pth doesn't list the user site) leaves Python's per-user site-packages on sys.path: ~/.local/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages on Linux, ~/Library/Python/X.Y/lib/python/site-packages for macOS framework builds, %APPDATA%\Python\PythonXY\site-packages on Windows. It's shared by every copy of X.Y for that user, and `pip install --user` writes there. To keep app copies isolated, launch with `-s` (or `-I`), or set PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html

recipes.notes: The .exe is a WiX Burn bundle (.wixburn section confirmed in 3.7.0, 3.8.0 and 3.14.7). Running it normally registers a Burn bundle plus one MSI product per component, so a second copy of the same version only offers Modify/Repair/Uninstall. Instead `/layout` writes the component MSIs (core.msi, exe.msi, lib.msi, ...) flat into a folder without installing anything, and `msiexec /a` (administrative install) unpacks each one. In common.wxs the InstallDirectory has no Name under TARGETDIR, so files land directly in {runtime_dir}; an admin install writes no registry keys and registers no product. Add doc/test to the MSI list if wanted. Skip launcher.msi (py.exe normally goes to %SystemRoot%), path.msi/appendpath.msi (PATH), ucrt.msi (a system update) and pip.msi (it only runs a custom action; ensurepip replaces it). What's lost: the py launcher, PEP 514 keys under HKLM\Software\Python\PythonCore\X.Y (wanted: TESTED-WINDOWS.md says a second registered Python conflicts), Start-menu shortcuts, .py file associations, a Programs and Features entry, Modify/Repair, and the optional precompile of the standard library (run `python -m compileall -q "{runtime_dir}\Lib"` if startup time matters). Risks: (1) the full installer embeds only the default MSIs. The docs say /layout fetches ALL components, including the *_d.msi/*_pdb.msi debug packages, from python.org. With no network, whether Burn still writes the embedded MSIs is UNVERIFIED (bpo-25126 is a related offline failure). The safest approach is to run /layout once at build time and ship the layout folder, or to extract the attached container with WiX `dark.exe -x`. (2) Don't let {runtime_dir} end in a backslash: `TARGETDIR="C:\x\"` escapes the quote. (3) TESTED-WINDOWS.md confirmed asyncio with the vendor installer run normally, not with this extraction, so re-test 3.7.0 on Vista and 3.8.0 on 7/8 with this method before relying on it. Relocation: python.exe finds its home from the Lib\os.py landmark next to it, so the folder can be moved or have spaces. Only the Scripts\*.exe launchers pip generates hold an absolute (quoted) python.exe path; `python -m <module>` always works. Registry leakage in: if a registered Python of the same X.Y exists, its PythonCore\X.Y\PythonPath subkeys can be added to sys.path. Adding a pythonXY._pth file (3.6+) stops that, but it also changes site/sys.path behaviour.

recipes.notes: These MSIs are built by CPython's own Tools/msi/msi.py, which defines an AdminExecuteSequence ('InitialTargetDir', 'SetDLLDirToTarget', and in 3.3/3.4 'SetLauncherDirToTarget'). So under `msiexec /a` pythonXY.dll and py.exe land in TARGETDIR rather than System32/%WINDIR%. 2.6/2.7 carry msvcr90.dll plus its manifest as a private-CRT file in the install root, and an admin install extracts it, so no VC++ 2008 redistributable is needed (not confirmed on a real XP). An admin install writes no registry keys (no PythonCore key, no .py association, no Programs and Features entry) and leaves a copy of the .msi in the root, which the second step deletes. What's lost: ensurepip and CompilePyc custom actions, shortcuts, file associations. 3.3/3.4 py.exe does land in the folder, but it isn't registered as the system launcher. 2.5.4 is ia64 (Itanium) only: same mechanism (2.5's msi.py has the same admin sequence), but its CRT handling (msvcr71 merge module) targets x86; untested and of little practical use. Old pip versions can no longer reach PyPI (TLS/SNI and index changes), so install packages from local wheels (`pip install --no-index --find-links`).

recipes.notes: TESTED on Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 with 3.14.7+20260901 install_only_stripped: unpacked twice side by side into '.../app one/rt' and '.../app two/rt' (paths with spaces). Both ran, with sys.prefix pointing at their own folder. ssl, sqlite3, ctypes, asyncio, tkinter (import), lzma, bz2 and readline all imported. `python -m pip install pyflakes` went into app one only. Moved 'app one' to 'app one moved': python3 and the shipped bin/pip3 still worked (PBS writes a relative `#!/bin/sh` + `exec "$(dirname -- "$(realpath -- "$0")")/python3.14"` shebang), but console scripts pip installed later (bin/pyflakes) hold the absolute old path and broke. So: relocatable as shipped; after moving, reinstall or rewrite shebangs of pip-installed scripts, or always call `python3 -m <module>`. Only other arches (arm64, armv7, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x) were not run. Known PBS quirk: `python3-config`/sysconfig report the build machine's compiler flags, so building C extensions may need CC overrides.

recipes.notes: TESTED with Python-2.7.18.tar.xz on Ubuntu 24.04 (gcc 13, OpenSSL 3.0.13). Building with --prefix containing a space FAILS at `make install` (Makefile install targets aren't quoted), so the recipe builds into a space-free temp prefix and copies the tree. The default build is a static libpython, and getpath finds its home from lib/python2.7/os.py, so copies in '.../app a/rt' and '.../app b/rt' each reported their own sys.prefix. ssl worked against system OpenSSL 3 (_ssl built); _hashlib did NOT build against OpenSSL 3, so hashlib falls back to the builtin md5/sha implementations. ensurepip installed pip 19.2.3 and setuptools 41.2.0, and pip wrote space-safe `#!/bin/sh` exec shebangs. But the shebangs of bin/pydoc, bin/idle, bin/2to3 and bin/python2.7-config point at the temp build prefix, so rewrite them with sed or use `python2.7 -m pydoc`. Not portable between distros: _ssl/_sqlite3/readline link to system .so versions (libssl.so.3 here). For a portable result, build on the oldest target distro, or link OpenSSL 1.1.1 statically (not tried). --enable-shared would add an RPATH problem; don't use it.

The binaries carry a code signature (whether ad-hoc or Developer ID was not checked); a plain tarball cannot carry a notarization ticket. If the downloaded tarball carries com.apple.quarantine (a browser download, or an installer app with LSFileQuarantineEnabled), Gatekeeper blocks the unpacked binaries, so the xattr step clears it. It's a no-op when the attribute is absent. The same shebang caveat as Linux applies to scripts pip installs later if the folder is moved.

steps.run: V=$(ls "{runtime_dir}/Python.framework/Versions" | grep -v Current); OLD="/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/$V"; cd "{runtime_dir}/Python.framework/Versions/$V" && for f in $(find . -type f -perm -u+x -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' -o -name Python); do file "$f" | grep -q Mach-O || continue; d=$(dirname "$f" | sed 's#^\./##; s#[^/][^/]*#..#g; s#^\.$##'); for l in $(otool -L "$f" | awk 'NR>1{print $1}' | grep "^$OLD"); do install_name_tool -change "$l" "@loader_path/${d:+$d/}${l#$OLD/}" "$f"; done; otool -D "$f" | grep -q "^$OLD" && install_name_tool -id "@rpath/${f#./}" "$f"; codesign -f -s - "$f" 2>/dev/null; done

prerequisites: install_name_tool and otool (Xcode Command Line Tools), which aren't in a stock macOS; or a Mach-O load-command patcher bundled with the base installer (the new paths are shorter than the old, so an in-place rewrite fits)
Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon (these builds are x86_64/i386 only)

recipes.notes: Inspected the files read-only: xar pkgs whose Python_Framework.pkg has install-location=/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework and relocatable=false, with a gzip cpio Payload. Other components: Applications (/Applications/Python X.Y), UnixTools (/usr/local/bin symlinks), Documentation, Shell_Profile_Updater (edits shell profiles), Install_Pip (postinstall runs ensurepip and symlinks pip into /usr/local/bin). Every Mach-O file references absolute /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/X.Y/... install names (the Python dylib, and lib/libssl/libcrypto/libtcl/libtk). So the extracted tree only runs after those are rewritten to @loader_path-relative paths. The stub bin/pythonX.Y finds Resources/Python.app via dladdr on the framework, and sys.prefix comes from the framework's location, so once the load paths are fixed it should run from any folder. Signing: the 3.7.6 macosx10.6 binaries have NO code signature; 2.7.18 macosx10.9 is signed, so rewriting breaks it, hence the ad-hoc `codesign -f -s -` (codesign ships with macOS). The step 3 script is a sketch and has NOT been run. The alternative is the vendor pkg: `installer -pkg {file} -target /` with a choices XML deselecting everything but the framework. That writes into /Library/Frameworks and pkgutil receipts, gives one copy per X.Y per machine and replaces an existing one (isolation: impossible).
